definition: Google Cloud Search (formerly known as Google Springboard) is an enterprise search tool integrated with Google Workspace.
details: It allows users to search for content in Google apps including Gmail, Google Docs, Google Drive, Google Calendar, Google Contacts, and Google Sites. It also provides “actionable information & recommendations” to users based on machine learning. In February 2017, Google Springboard was renamed Google Cloud Search.

explainer.lead: Google Cloud Search is a search tool for finding information across a company’s Google Workspace apps. It can also use machine learning to offer actionable information and recommendations, reducing the need to check each app separately.

tiers.eli5: Imagine having one library helper who can look through your email, documents, calendar, contacts, and other work materials instead of you opening every drawer. You ask what you need, and Google Cloud Search helps find it across Google Workspace. It can also suggest useful information using machine learning.
tiers.practitioner: Use Cloud Search as a unified search interface over supported Google Workspace content, including Gmail, Docs, Drive, Calendar, Contacts, and Sites. Its machine-learning features can supplement query results with actionable information and recommendations. It should be evaluated as enterprise Workspace search, not as a replacement for public web search or as a guarantee that every recommendation will be relevant.
tiers.paperLevel: Let q be a user query and C be the content available in supported Google Workspace applications; Google Cloud Search maps q to matching items in C and can additionally produce machine-learning-based actionable information and recommendations. The product was formerly called Google Springboard and was renamed Google Cloud Search in February 2017.

explainer.example: An employee trying to resume a project can search for its name in Cloud Search rather than opening each app separately. Relevant material may come from a project document in Docs, a stored file in Drive, or a related message in Gmail, with additional recommendations where available.

explainer.intuition: Instead of treating each Workspace app as a separate place to search, Cloud Search gives users one entry point to their enterprise content. Machine learning adds suggestions and actionable information beyond simply locating items.
howItWorks: A user enters a search request in Google Cloud Search.
Cloud Search looks across supported Google Workspace apps for relevant content.
Results can include material from Gmail, Docs, Drive, Calendar, Contacts, and Sites.
Machine learning can also provide actionable information and recommendations.
explainer.whyItMatters: Work information is often spread across several applications, so searching each one separately costs time and can miss useful context. Cloud Search brings those searches together and adds machine-learning-based assistance.
misconceptions: It is not simply the public Google web search applied to a company; it is an enterprise search tool integrated with Google Workspace.
It is not limited to Google Drive: the supported apps also include Gmail, Docs, Calendar, Contacts, and Sites.
Google Springboard is its former name, not a separate current product described here.
